judges.16.p1.b1.text: One day Samson went to Gaza, where he saw a prostitute and went in to spend the night with her.

judges.16.p1.b3.text: they surrounded that place and lay in wait for him all night at the city gate.

judges.16.p1.b4.text: Let us wait until dawn; then we will kill him.

judges.16.p2.b1.text: But Samson lay there only until midnight, when he got up,

judges.16.p2.b2.text: took hold of the doors of the city gate and both gateposts, and pulled them out, bar and all.

judges.16.p2.b3.text: Then he put them on his shoulders and took them to the top of the mountain overlooking Hebron.

judges.16.p3.b1.text: Some time later, Samson fell in love with a woman in the Valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.

judges.16.p3.b2.text: Entice him and find out the source of his great strength and how we can overpower him to tie him up and subdue him.

judges.16.p3.b3.text: Then each one of us will give you eleven hundred shekels of silver.

judges.16.p4.b1.text: Please tell me the source of your great strength and how you can be tied up and subdued.

judges.16.p4.b2.text: If they tie me up with seven fresh bowstrings that have not been dried, I will become as weak as any other man.

judges.16.p4.b3.text: she tied him up with them. While the men were hidden in her room,

judges.16.p4.b5.text: But he snapped the bowstrings like a strand of yarn seared by a flame.

judges.16.p5.b1.text: You have mocked me and lied to me! Now please tell me how you can be tied up.

judges.16.p5.b2.text: If they tie me up with new ropes that have never been used, I will become as weak as any other man.

judges.16.p5.b3.text: he snapped the ropes off his arms like they were threads.

judges.16.p5.b4.text: If you weave the seven braids of my head into the web of a loom and tighten it with a pin,

judges.16.p5.b6.text: pulled out the pin with the loom and the web.

judges.16.p6.b1.text: How can you say, ‘I love you,’ … when your heart is not with me? This is the third time you have mocked me …

judges.16.p6.b2.text: Finally, after she had pressed him daily with her words and pleaded until he was sick to death,

judges.16.p6.b3.text: My hair has never been cut, because I have been a Nazirite to God from my mother’s womb.

judges.16.p6.b4.text: If I am shaved, my strength will leave me, …

judges.16.p7.b1.text: Come up once more, for he has revealed to me all that is in his heart.

judges.16.p7.b2.text: Then the lords of the Philistines came to her, bringing the money in their hands.

judges.16.p7.b3.text: And having lulled him to sleep on her lap,

judges.16.p7.b4.text: she called a man to shave off the seven braids of his head.

judges.16.p7.b5.text: In this way she began to subdue him, and his strength left him.

judges.16.p8.b2.text: I will escape as I did before and shake myself free. …

judges.16.p8.b3.text: But he did not know that the LORD had departed from him.

judges.16.p8.b4.text: Then the Philistines seized him, … and brought him down to Gaza, where he was bound with bronze shackles

judges.16.p9.b1.text: gouged out his eyes, … and forced to grind grain in the prison.

judges.16.p9.b2.text: However, the hair of his head began to grow back after it had been shaved.

judges.16.p10.b1.text: Now the lords of the Philistines gathered together to offer a great sacrifice to their god Dagon. They rejoiced

judges.16.p10.b2.text: Our god has delivered Samson our enemy into our hands.

judges.16.p10.b3.text: Call for Samson to entertain us.

judges.16.p10.b4.text: So they called Samson out of the prison to entertain them.

judges.16.p11.b1.text: Lead me where I can feel the pillars supporting the temple, so I can lean against them.

judges.16.p11.b2.text: about three thousand men and women were on the roof watching Samson entertain them.

judges.16.p11.b3.text: O Lord GOD, please remember me. Strengthen me, O God, just once more,

judges.16.p11.b4.text: And Samson reached out for the two central pillars supporting the temple. Bracing himself against them with his right hand on one pillar and his left hand on the other,

judges.16.p12.b1.text: Let me die with the Philistines.

judges.16.p12.b2.text: Then he pushed with all his might, and the temple fell on the lords and all the people in it.

judges.16.p12.b3.text: carried him back, and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of his father Manoah. And he had judged Israel twenty years.
